title: Week of Aug 31 – Sep 6 · Foundations Week 2: Two Real Lifts a Day
subtitle: Same four strength nights and two easy runs — but each lift day now opens with TWO main lifts instead of one, and the back strength you asked for is officially in the program.
goals: The big change: every lift day starts with two main lifts, both with warm-up sets and real targets. Last week each day had one; you earned the second one by making all your sessions and pushing the squat to 75 on your own
Back strength is in, per your journal ('I want to add more back strength'): barbell rows debut Thursday, the lat pulldown carries a heavier target, and rows stay in the rotation
Squat moves to 70 for all sets — the honest middle between the 75 you hit at your limit Monday and the 65s from Thursday. Smooth 8s at 70 beat one grinding set at 75

The runs didn't happen last week (a sculpt class stepped in Friday — logged, and it counts). Both easy runs are back this week: 2 miles max, conversational, knee report in the log. The 🚴 swap is right there if it complains
Hips and core stay the quiet main event — three hip flexor touches and 6 core sets every lift night, same as before. Your 4/10 hips-and-thighs soreness after sculpt says it's all working
Still on the list: connect Strava at workoutplanning-production.up.railway.app/api/strava/connect/emma so runs and heart rate show up automatically
review: Week 1 verdict: three of four lifts made, every logged session complete top to bottom, and a squat that went 65 → 75 because you decided it had more in it ('at my limit but good'). That's exactly the week this plan wanted. The plan of attack for week 2, built from your log: Brendan asked for a second main lift on each of your strength days, so now every session opens with two barbell-or-dumbbell lifts that get warm-up sets and targets — squat and bench Monday, RDL (now on the barbell) and overhead press Tuesday, squat and a new barbell row Thursday, bench and RDL again Saturday. Your 'more back strength' note is why the row is here. Weights all start from what you actually logged — nothing jumps more than one small step. Saturday didn't get logged and the runs got skipped, so this week the goal is simple: all four lifts AND both little runs. Soreness from sculpt plus lifting is normal; drop the last set of anything if it piles up and carry on.

days.name: Foundation A · Squat + Bench
warmup: 5 min easy cardio (bike, row, or brisk walk)

items.note: 70 for all three sets. Last Monday you went 65/65/75 and called 75 your limit — 70 across the board is the earned middle. If all three sets are smooth 8s, 75 for everything next week.
items.focus: Brace, chest tall, knees track over toes, squat to a depth you control.

items.note: Main lift #2, new this week: the barbell version of the press you've been doing. Start with just the bar (45) — it'll feel different from dumbbells even though you've pressed more than this. Learn the path this week, add weight next. If no rack is free, DB bench at last week's weight is a full substitute.
items.focus: Shoulder blades set, feet planted, lower to mid-chest, press up and slightly back.

items.note: 15s, where you finished last week — and part of the back-strength push you asked for. If set 3 is strict and easy, grab the 20.
items.focus: Flat back, pull to your hip, squeeze the shoulder blade.

items.note: The hips block, same as last week — this is the hip flexor strength work. No band? March slowly in place driving each knee above hip height with a 1s hold.
items.focus: Low back stays glued to the floor on the march; toes forward and hip stacked on the leg lifts.

items.note: Core block, 6 sets: dead bug → plank, three rounds, ~20s between moves.
items.focus: Ribs down, low back pressed into the floor, opposite arm and leg reach long.

items.note: Add ~5–10s over last week's holds if they were solid.
items.focus: Straight line head to heels, glutes tight, breathe — don't hold your breath.

stretches: Kneeling hip flexor stretch — 45s each side

days.name: Foundation B · Barbell RDL + Press
warmup: 5 min easy cardio (bike, row, or brisk walk)

items.note: Graduation: last week's dumbbell RDLs (you worked up to 25s) move to the barbell. Start at 65 — bar plus small plates. The hinge is the same one you practiced; the bar just sits closer and feels more stable. RPE 6–7, hamstrings talking, back never.
items.focus: Soft knees, hips back, bar sliding down the thighs, flat back the whole way.

items.note: Main lift #2 tonight, promoted to a real slot: 15s like last week, and if set 1 is an easy 10, take the next size up for sets 2–3.
items.focus: Ribs down, press straight up, finish with biceps by your ears.

items.note: 35 — one small step up from last week's 30, deliberately lighter than Monday's barbell work.
items.focus: Elbows inside the knees at the bottom, tall chest, drive up through the whole foot.

items.note: The hips block — your knee insurance, same as last week. Band optional on the clamshells.
items.focus: Bridges: drive through the heel, hips level. Clamshells: slow, toes together, don't let the hip roll back.

items.note: Core block, 6 sets: side plank → bird dog, three rounds. From the knees is still a fine version.
items.focus: Hips stacked and lifted, straight line shoulder to feet.
Slow reach, hips square to the floor, pause 2s at full stretch.

stretches: Kneeling hip flexor stretch — 45s each side

days.name: Easy Run · 2 mi (or Bike)
warmup: Ankle circles + a few walking lunges

run.title: Easy conversational run — take two
run.detail: This one slipped last week, so it's the week's honest goal: two easy miles at full-sentence pace, walk breaks completely fine. It's also still the knee test read — note how it feels during and after. A little awareness that fades is okay; real pain or a changed stride means stop and tap the 🚴 toggle instead. Legs will carry Monday and Tuesday's lifting; slower is correct.

hr.zone: Easy / conversational (RPE 3–4) — connect Strava and future runs get HR zones
hr.main: RPE 3–4 — full sentences the whole way
hr.note: The lifting is what's pushing this week. Runs are practice moving, nothing more.

stretches: Kneeling hip flexor stretch — 45s each side

days.name: Foundation C · Squat + Barbell Row
warmup: 5 min easy cardio (bike, row, or brisk walk)

items.note: Second exposure: 70 again, aiming for these to look identical to Monday's. Last Thursday you kept it at 65 — if Monday's 70s were smooth, these should feel familiar, not scary.
items.focus: Same cues as Monday: brace, chest tall, controlled depth.

items.note: Main lift #2 and the headline answer to your 'more back strength' note. Start with just the bar (45): hinge like your RDL, hold that angle, and pull the bar to your lower ribs. This plus pulldowns plus rows is a real back program now.
items.focus: Flat back held still, pull with the elbows, squeeze the shoulder blades, no heaving.

items.note: 50 — you finished there last week, so it's the working weight now. 55 if the last rep of set 1 is smooth.
items.focus: Chest up, pull the bar to your collarbone, elbows down and back — no leaning way back.

items.note: You added 5s last week — keep them, or 10s if the knee stays quiet. Still the knee-friendly lunge.
items.focus: Long stride back, tall torso, drive through the front heel to stand.

items.n: Hip Flexor Raise + Leg Raise superset
items.note: The hips block: standing knee drives with a 2s hold (add a light ankle weight or band when 8 gets easy), then 10 slow straight-leg raises. 3 rounds.
items.focus: Stand tall — no leaning back to cheat the knee up. On leg raises, low back stays pressed to the floor.

items.note: Core block, 6 sets: hollow hold → shoulder taps, three rounds. Bend the knees to shorten the lever if your low back arches.
items.focus: Low back pressed down, ribs pulled in, arms and legs only as long as you can control.
Feet a bit wider, hips dead still — the tap is the easy part, the not-rocking is the exercise.

stretches: Kneeling hip flexor stretch — 45s each side

days.name: Rest Day (Sculpt Counts)
days.desc: Rest, earned again. Last Friday's sculpt class was a great use of this slot — 4/10 sore in exactly the muscles this plan is building — so same deal: sculpt, a gentle walk, or easy hip stretching all fit here, or nothing at all. Just log whatever happens.
fields: What did you do? (fine if nothing)
How sore are you, 1–10, and where?

days.name: Foundation D · Bench + RDL, Round Two
warmup: 5 min easy cardio (bike, row, or brisk walk)
Arm circles + band pull-aparts (or wall slides) — 10 each
Banded lateral walks (or side steps) — 10 each way

items.note: Second exposure to the bar. Same 45 as Monday unless every set was an easy 8 — then 50. This Saturday didn't get logged last week; make this the one that does.
items.focus: Shoulder blades set, controlled lowering, press up and slightly back.

items.note: Second hinge of the week: same 65 as Tuesday, aim for smoother reps. Two exposures a week is how the pattern sticks.
items.focus: Soft knees, hips back, bar close, hamstrings load, flat back.

items.note: A dumbbell across your hips (folded towel for comfort), pause 1s at the top of every rep.
items.focus: Drive through the heels, squeeze the glutes to lift, ribs down at the top — no low-back arch.

items.note: The hips block: banded side-steps into the psoas march. Third hip flexor touch of the week — the muscle you asked to build still gets its frequency.
items.focus: Stay low in a quarter-squat on the walks; slow controlled knee drives on the march.

items.note: Core block, 6 sets: plank → side plank, three rounds.
items.focus: Straight line head to heels, glutes tight, breathe.
Hips stacked and lifted the whole time; from the knees is fine.

stretches: Kneeling hip flexor stretch — 45s each side

days.name: Short Easy Run · 1.5–2 mi (or Bike / Walk)
warmup: Ankle circles + a few walking lunges

run.title: Easy shakeout to close the week
run.detail: Run number two: 1.5–2 miles, genuinely easy, daylight if you like. Same knee rule as Wednesday — note how it behaves during and after, and the 🚴 bike or a long walk closes the week just as well. Then look back: if both runs and all four lifts happened, that's the first full week of the new plan in the books, with two real lifts a night.

hr.main: RPE 3–4 — you should be able to talk in full sentences
hr.cool: 5 min walk, then stretch while warm
hr.note: After a 4-lift week your legs will be tired. Slower than feels necessary is exactly right.

stretches: Kneeling hip flexor stretch — 60s each side
